name: Chili Crisp Noodle Salad

cookwares.name: large pot; colander or fine-mesh strainer

ingredients.name: chili crisp, plus more for serving
scallions, trimmed and thinly sliced crosswise
chopped fresh cilantro, plus more for serving

instructions.primary_message: In a large colander, combine cucumbers, salt, and 1 teaspoon sugar and toss to combine. Let sit until cucumbers release their liquid, about 20 minutes. Set aside.

While cucumbers are draining, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook noodles until tender, following timing on package's instructions. Drain in a colander and rinse with cold running water until chilled.
Meanwhile, in a large bowl, whisk tahini, vinegar or lime juice, chili crisp, soy sauce, and remaining 2 teaspoons sugar until smooth. Gradually add water while whisking constantly.
Add scallions, cilantro, drained cucumbers, and noodles to tahini mixture. Mix gently to coat cucumbers and noodles.
Transfer noodles to serving bowls. Top with chili crisp, cilantro, and peanuts or sesame seeds, if using. Serve.

schema_metadata.keywords: noodle salad, chili crisp, chili crisp noodle salad, chili crisp noodles, sesame noodles, cold sesame noodles, pasta salad

description: Ready in less than 30 minutes, this chili crisp noodle salad combines soba noodles, crunchy cucumbers, and a creamy, spicy dressing.
notes:
Optional or for serving: Chopped roasted salted peanuts or toasted sesame seeds, for serving (optional)

Optional substitutions: rice wine vinegar → fresh lime juice

Make-ahead and storage: The tahini–chili crisp sauce can be made up to 4 days in advance.
Leftovers can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 4 days, though the noodles will become soggier over time.
author: Laila Ibrahim
